items.question: How long does it take to build an agent?
items.answer: A working first version usually takes less than a month. Getting it into production with your data, permissions and approvals takes around three months. From there it grows with your needs.

items.question: What return can we expect, and how do you measure it?
items.answer: Before we build anything, we measure how long the task takes today and how often it runs. After launch we measure again. The return is the time saved multiplied by the cost of that time, minus what the agent costs to run. If the numbers do not justify an agent, we tell you.

items.question: Do you build custom agents or use ready-made ones?
items.answer: Both. Where a ready-made tool does the job, we set it up and connect it. Where your process is specific, we build a custom agent around it. The choice depends on what gets you the result fastest and cheapest.

items.question: Where is our data processed, and is it used for training?
items.answer: We use enterprise AI plans whose terms exclude training on your data. Where your rules require it, we host models and data on infrastructure you control. Processing follows the GDPR, and we document where every piece of data goes.

items.question: What happens after launch?
items.answer: We monitor the agent, fix what breaks and improve it as your process changes. You can keep us on a support plan or take it over fully.

items.question: Can our team maintain the agents ourselves?
items.answer: Yes. We work alongside your team, document everything and train the people who will own the agent, so you are never locked in.

ai-agents.intro: An agent is software that can read, check and act across several systems, the way an assistant would, but in minutes and without getting tired. We design the agent around one of your real processes, connect it to your tools and make sure a person approves anything that matters before it leaves.

jointForces.title: Two brains, one product. It has worked before.
jointForces.intro: Firms with deep expertise are already turning their know-how into AI products with a tech partner. Here is what came out of it.

items.story: A global law firm brought its precedents and negotiating know-how. An AI startup and Microsoft brought the technology. Together they built ContractMatrix, a contract tool the firm now sells to its clients.
items.result: Over 1,000 of the firm's lawyers used it from launch, saving about seven hours on some contract negotiations.

items.story: PwC's tax experts curated the data, annotated examples and reviewed the answers. Harvey's engineers built the model. The result is an AI tax assistant shaped by PwC's own method.
items.result: In a blind test, PwC's experts preferred its answers 91% of the time over other AI tools.

items.story: Drug developers brought decades of clinical trial know-how. OpenAI brought the models. Together they built Muse, a tool that plans how to recruit patients for trials.
items.result: According to the companies, it cuts that planning from months to minutes.

consulting-firms.intro: Your clients ask for AI agents. You know their business better than anyone, but building agents is not your trade. It is ours. Together we turn your method into a co-branded AI product for your sector, owned by both of us.

why.title: Your clients want AI. Advice on paper is no longer enough.

items.title: Clients will ask someone
items.text: Digitalisation is on every board agenda. A firm that brings only slides and recommendations loses the next mandate to one that ships working tools.

items.title: An AI team takes years to build
items.text: Hiring engineers, choosing tools, securing data and keeping systems running is a business of its own. You should not have to start it from zero.

items.title: Partnering beats building alone
items.text: In MIT's 2025 study of AI in business, tools built with an outside partner made it past the pilot and into real use about 67% of the time. Tools built in-house: about 33%.

bring.title: Two kinds of know-how. One product.
bring.intro: Think of an architect and a builder. One knows what the house must be, the other knows how to make it stand. Neither builds a great house alone.

you.title: You bring the business brain
items: Your method: frameworks, checklists, templates and the way you work
Deep knowledge of your sector and its rules
Your client relationships and the trust behind them
The judgement on what a good answer looks like

items: AI agents and multi-step agent systems, designed, built and hosted

Skills for the agent, open source or built for you, and the data behind them
Security, monitoring and 99% uptime in production
Maintenance and new versions as AI moves on

together.title: Together: your method, as a product.
together.text: A co-branded AI agent your firm can offer to every client in your sector. You go from selling hours to selling a digital product, and you digitalise your own firm along the way. We grow together: your expertise makes our engineering useful, our engineering makes your expertise scale. Both of us own what we create.

steps.title: From first call to a product in production

items.title: Partner call
items.text: We learn how your firm works, which problem your clients pay you to solve, and where an agent would earn its keep.

items.title: Your method, mapped
items.text: You share your frameworks, documents and examples of good work. We turn them into the agent's knowledge, rules and tools.

items.title: First working agent
items.text: A working prototype, not slides. You try it on a real case.

items.title: Teach and test, together
items.text: We go back and forth. You review the answers, we adjust, until you say the output is what you would deliver yourself.

items.title: Live in production
items.text: The agent runs securely, connected to the tools it needs, monitored, with 99% uptime.

items.title: Launch and grow together
items.text: We bring the product to your clients under both brands, learn from real use and keep improving it.

items.question: Do we need technical staff?
items.answer: No. We handle the design, build, hosting, security and maintenance. Your team brings the method and reviews the output.

items.question: Who owns the product?
items.answer: We create it together and both own it. The exact terms, including what each of us can do with it later, are set in a partnership agreement before we start.

items.question: How do we teach the agent our way of working?
items.answer: You share your documents, frameworks and examples. We turn them into the agent's knowledge and rules, then test it with you case by case until the answers meet your standard. After launch you can keep updating its knowledge yourself.

items.question: Can we offer it to several clients?
items.answer: Yes, that is the idea. We build one product for your sector, then set it up for each client with their own data and tools.

items.question: What happens to our clients' data?
items.answer: Each client's data stays separate. We agree with every client where their data is stored and who can see it, and we sign a confidentiality agreement before any data is shared.

items.question: What kind of agents can we build?
items.answer: Anything your method can describe: assistants that answer from your knowledge base, agents that draft reports, audits or proposals, or multi-step systems that work inside your clients' tools.
